newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close lower amid political scandal.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close lower amid political scandal.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed lower on Thursday as uncertainty dominated the market in the wake of a political scandal that threatens to bring down the government, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: -0.02 pct to 105.16
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.01 at 105.18
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.11 pct to 105.16
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.03 to 105.25
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 to 104.15
Volume was 163 million shekels.
"There is uncertainty in the market. The political situation is such that economic issues will not be at the centre of the government's attention," said a trader at a big financial company.
"Traders fear interest rates will stay the same or even rise and that the government will not tackle inflation," he said.
Police said on Wednesday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should be charged with fraud and breach of trust in an influence-peddling scandal.
An aide to Netanyahu said on Thursday he did not believe the state prosecutor would implement the police recommendation.

"Prices were up on short-term CPI-linked bonds because of the higher than expected (March) consumer price index (CPI)," said the trader. "But prices of CPI-linked bonds longer than seven years were down on fears that maybe interest rates will rise, forcing up yields," he said.
The March CPI rose 1.0 percent against analysts' expectations for a 0.7 percent increase.
"Prices of unlinked bonds continued to fall across the board following March's high CPI," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
Prices of the dollar-linked bonds were stable after days of gains on the strengthening of the dollar worldwide.

The shekel fell sharply against the dollar on Thursday in the wake of the scandal and the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4040 against 3.3980 on Wednesday. Traders said dollar-bonds generally react a day later to the closing price of the shekel.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.4 shekels)
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
